id: EST1b: two literature estimators in the same closed loop - does their hold-entry latency alone predict their holdable force? (extension of EST1)
registered: 2026-11-04, before any EST1b run on the registered seeds; EST1 (OR/SM/MB) is registered separately and runs on the same seeds. Smoke test (seed 1300, 45 N fore-aft, one run each): both held; entry 10 ms (EM) and 15 ms (CI); quiet raw noise EM 3.8-3.9 N, CI 2.5-2.6 N, ours 4.6-5.2 N, MOB 2.3-2.4 N.

arms.EM: enhanced momentum observer after Sun et al. 2026 (lead + constant-velocity Kalman filter on the lower-body momentum observer; measurement noise matched to our quiet-stance noise in ESTCMP2, R = 1584.9, process noise 4e5, lead 1/K): RA_EST_ALT=emo
arms.CI: centroidal estimate with the IMU but without joint accelerations after Fedsi et al. 2026: RA_EST_ALT=cimu
arms.common: same controller, information paths, release rule (capture prediction only), forces and seeds as EST1; reference boundary and entry latency = EST1 arm OR

predictions.E1b latency predicts the boundary: for EM and CI in each direction: |boundary / boundary(OR) - exp(-omega dL)| <= 0.08, dL = median entry latency minus that of OR (EST1)
predictions.reported: boundaries and entry latencies of EM and CI against SM and MB (no directional prediction)
